modelChoice: qwen_audio_tts was tried FIRST because it advertises `ko` and exposes speech_rate/pitch_rate/instruction knobs. Every voice id from `higgsfield voices list` is rejected by it at generate time with 'Voice preset is not available for Qwen Audio' [OBSERVED 2026-08-09] — the shared 114-voice catalog and that model's voice_id parameter are different namespaces, and the CLI surfaces no qwen-compatible ids. inworld_text_to_speech carries its own voice enum with four Korean voices and works, at the cost of exposing prompt+voice only (no rate/pitch/style).
postProcessing: The API returns 48 kHz mono PCM WAV under a .mp3 filename (codec pcm_s16le, 768 kbps — the extension lies about the contents). Each file was transcoded to real MP3 at 96 kbps mono / 44.1 kHz, matching the per-channel budget of the existing 128 kbps stereo cues: 3,145,536 -> 371,810 bytes, 88.2% smaller with no audible loss on speech. Everything under Resources/ ships in the WebGL build, so the raw PCM would have cost 3 MB of the 120 MB cap for 30 seconds of dialogue.
